name: backthread
description: Backthread keeps the thread on what your AI coding agent ships — it captures the why behind every change and turns it into a living 'How it works' view of your codebase you can actually query.
author: Backthread
comment: PUBLISHED BIN = the self-contained esbuild bundle (dist-bundle/backthread.js), NOT the tsc dist/. Reason: @backthread/redact ships SOURCE-ONLY (.ts), and Node refuses to strip types for files inside node_modules — so a registry install of the tsc dist/ would fail to load redact at runtime. The bundle inlines redact (and the MCP SDK), so the published CLI has ZERO runtime dependencies and `npx backthread` stays fast and robust. Dev/test resolve @backthread/redact via the workspace symlink (realpath escapes node_modules → stripping applies).
comment_test_isolation: `--experimental-test-isolation=none` runs every test file in ONE process instead of forking one child per file — see the matching note in packages/extractor/package.json for why. Short version: the forked runner reconstructs its report by scanning each child's stdout for v8 frame headers, and a pipe-chunk boundary in the wrong place makes it fail with `Unable to deserialize cloned data` against a test file that passed. In-process, there is no child and no framing to get wrong.

scripts.prepack: npm run build && npm run bundle
scripts.smoke: npm run bundle && node dist-bundle/backthread.js help > /dev/null
scripts.test: node --import tsx --test --experimental-test-isolation=none --test-force-exit src/*.test.ts && npm run build && npm run smoke
